skills.trigger: When evaluating tracheal deviation on a chest X-ray to determine the underlying etiology (mass effect vs. volume loss vs. pleural pathology).
steps: Identify the direction of tracheal displacement by tracing the air column from the cervical region down to the carina relative to the spinous processes.
Inspect the ipsilateral hemithorax (same side as deviation) for a discrete soft-tissue opacity or widened mediastinum that physically pushes structures away (mass effect).
Inspect the contralateral hemithorax for signs of volume loss, such as elevated hemidiaphragm, crowded ribs, or opaque lung fields (atelectasis), which would pull the trachea toward it.
Evaluate the costophrenic angles and lung periphery for meniscus signs (effusion) or visceral pleural lines with absent lung markings (pneumothorax) to rule out pleural causes.

Correlate the finding of a prominent paratracheal/mediastinal mass displacing the trachea away from the lesion with lymphoproliferative disorders like Hodgkin Lymphoma, distinguishing it from atelectasis which pulls the trachea toward the opacity.
